conductSummary: Knowingly administering a controlled substance to another, or inducing or causing its use, by force, threat or deception. Division (B) excludes specified lawful professional conduct.
gradeSummary: For Schedule I/II other than marihuana and the five specifically listed compounds: F2, or F1 in the vicinity of a school, with mandatory prison. For Schedule III/IV/V: F2 in both settings; prison is presumed ordinarily and mandatory near a school. For marihuana or a compound listed in (C)(3): F4 ordinarily, F3 near a school, with §2929.13(C) governing prison. Division (E) provides a separate mandatory prison term in lieu of the ordinary term for the specified Schedule I/II sale, offer or possession, court finding of major-drug-offender status, and §2941.1410(A) specification. Division (E) cites §2929.14(B)(3)(a); the retained sentencing section numbers the pertinent paragraph (B)(3). An exact individual term under that special branch requires separate review. For F1, F2 and F3 Chapter 2925 convictions, §2929.18(B)(1) generally requires a fine of at least half the maximum, unless a timely indigency affidavit and court finding of inability to pay satisfy the statutory exception. Professional-license notice may apply under §2925.38. Under §2929.33 a vehicle used to further the offense may trigger license suspension; a qualifying same-circumstances impaired-driving conviction or plea requires suspension for up to five years.

conductSummary: Knowingly engaging in one of four juvenile-related acts. For (a) through (c) the juvenile must be at least two years younger, with knowledge of age or recklessness: furnishing or administering a controlled substance, inducing its use, or inducing a felony drug abuse offense. Division (d) separately covers using a juvenile for surveillance to prevent detection or arrest for a felony drug abuse offense, irrespective of knowledge of age. The two-year gap belongs only to (a) through (c). Division (B) excludes specified lawful professional conduct.
